## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dasasikkhāpada* (or *Dasa Sikkhāpadāni*) is the second text in the *Khuddakapāṭha* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral; Hazra 1994; Williams & Ladwig 2012]. It sets out the code of ten ethical precepts or training rules prescribed for novice monastics (*sāmaṇera*) upon receiving the going-forth (*pabbajjā*) [SuttaCentral; Hazra 1982; Hazra 1994]. These rules require abstention from: (1) taking life, (2) stealing, (3) unchastity, (4) false speech, (5) drinking intoxicants, (6) eating at improper times, (7) dancing, music, and attending shows, (8) using garlands, perfumes, and bodily adornments, (9) using high or luxurious beds, and (10) accepting gold and silver [Hazra 1994; Pranke]. Monastic ritual manuals note that novices undertake these rules with the recitation of individual training clauses (*pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṁ samādiyāmi*, etc.) concluded by the collective formula *imāni dasa sikkhāpadāni samādiyāmi* [Vinayamukha 1983]. Maurice Winternitz noted that this foundational code of monastic morality represents an early stratum of rules likely tracing back to the Buddha himself [Winternitz 1933].
Beyond novice ordination, the *Dasasikkhāpada* functions as a fundamental liturgical text across Theravāda traditions [Williams & Ladwig 2012]. It is regularly included at the beginning of the *Catubhāṇavāra* paritta collection and Southeast Asian recitation manuscripts, placed directly following the Three Refuges (*Saraṇattaya* or *Tisaraṇa*) and preceding the *Dvattiṁsākāra* and *Kumārapañha* (or *Sāmaṇerapañha*) [Kalupahana 2001; Anālayo 2018; Walker].
